diagnosis_explanation: Your brain has two sides. The right side of your brain was affected by a stroke. This means that part of your brain has been injured. It can affect how you move, speak, or understand things. This is called a right hemisphere disorder.
medication_rationale: Your doctor did not give you any new medicines to take at home. Ask at your next visit if you need to start any.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will feel tired and may have trouble focusing. This is normal.
- Rest is important. Take short breaks during the day.
- You can practice looking for things on a page.
- Try to recall the main idea of a story you hear.
- Call your doctor if you have a sudden headache or confusion.
- Your goal is to rest and take care of yourself at home.

**Week 2:**
- Your energy levels may start to slowly increase.
- You can try doing simple tasks around the house.
- Practice listening to short stories and remember key details.
- Work on tasks that need you to focus for 15 minutes.
- If you feel confused, take a break and rest.
- Your goal is to complete one task that needs focus each day.

**Week 3:**
- You may feel a bit more like yourself this week.
- Try reading short articles or simple books.
- Work on remembering the main idea and details from what you read.
- Continue practicing tasks that require sustained attention.
- Call your doctor if you have trouble speaking or understanding speech.
- Your goal is to read for 10 minutes and recall details.

**Week 4:**
- You should notice steady progress in your thinking skills.
- Try to do tasks that require sustained attention for longer periods.
- Continue practicing visual scanning and recall exercises.
- You can try to recall the main idea plus five details after a delay.
- Call your doctor if you experience sudden vision changes.
- Your goal is to complete a sustained attention task for 20 minutes.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Recovery takes time, so be patient with yourself.
- Keep practicing the skills you learned in therapy.
- Celebrate small wins and acknowledge your progress.
- Continue to follow up with your healthcare team.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Sudden severe headache: This could be a brain bleed.
- Trouble speaking or loss of words: This is a stroke sign.
- Vision loss or double vision: This may be a stroke sign.
- Weakness on one side of body: This is a stroke sign.
- Numbness on one side of body: This is a stroke sign.
- Trouble walking or loss of balance: This is a stroke sign.
- Sudden confusion or trouble understanding: This is a stroke sign.
- Seizure: Call 911 right away.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Worsening headache: Your pain is getting worse.
- Trouble seeing or double vision: Your vision is changing.
- Numbness or weakness: This is on one side.
- Trouble walking or loss of balance: This is a fall risk.
- Confusion or trouble understanding: Your thinking is changing.
- Dizziness and spinning feeling: This is vertigo.
- Feeling very tired or sleepy: You may need rest.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild headache: Your pain is not severe.
- Trouble remembering things: Your memory is affected.
- Mild numbness or tingling: This is a light feeling.
- Slight trouble with balance: You feel a little unsteady.
- Fatigue that is improving: You are feeling better.
- Feeling down or sad: Your mood is low.
- Trouble sleeping: Rest is hard to find.
